summary: The activations come from a real sigmoid forward pass for every supported size. The backward pulses and changing wire widths illustrate training, but they do not calculate a loss gradient.

claims.claim: Each neuron applies an activation to a weighted sum.
claims.how: Every layer is checked independently as sigmoid of the incoming weighted sum plus its bias, including the default 3-4-2 network.

sources.title: Multilayer perceptrons
sources.says: Hidden layers with nonlinear activations extend the functions a linear classifier can represent.

claims.claim: The size controls choose a small multilayer network.
claims.how: The 108 control combinations stay within the 14-neuron cap and use the same forward calculation.

sources.title: Multilayer perceptrons
sources.says: Hidden layers with nonlinear activations extend the functions a linear classifier can represent.

claims.claim: Backward pulses and wire changes are a prepared training illustration.
claims.how: Wire changes use a repeating index-based pattern; no target, loss, chain rule, or updated forward pass is used.

sources.title: Backpropagation
sources.says: Backpropagation applies the chain rule to compute loss gradients for network parameters.

claims.note: The About text already identifies the prepared example. A real training view would need a loss and gradients.

simplified: Inputs and weights are deterministic examples. The apparent backward update uses fixed wire changes rather than backpropagation; the total size is capped at 14 neurons.

fixes.what: A future training view could compute a loss, backpropagate its derivatives, and show the changed forward prediction.
